headline: Operating profit rises on investment income; net falls
summary_short: W. R. Berkley's Q3 2026 net income was $446.0M ($1.14 per share) versus $511.0M ($1.28), while operating income per share rose 6% to $1.17 and net investment income hit $383.5M.
summary_long: The drop in net income reflects $17.5M of net investment losses against $78.8M of gains a year ago. Operating return on equity was 18.8% and the reported combined ratio was 90.8%, with a 88.1% accident-year ratio before catastrophes. Insurance segment pre-tax underwriting income grew 10.6% to $237.7M on 3.2% net premium growth. Average rate increases excluding workers' compensation were about 4.0%. Year-to-date the company returned $728.6M to shareholders, including $435.1M of buybacks.
confidence_notes: Operating income and operating ROE are non-GAAP as defined by W. R. Berkley. Net income and net investment income y/y changes computed from the release's table (446,005 vs 511,032; 383,537 vs 351,238). Combined ratio comparison to the prior year is not in the extracted text.

drivers.explanation: The CEO credits rate adequacy and terms-and-conditions discipline in underwriting, plus a strong investment portfolio.
Growth was driven by a 12.0% increase in the core portfolio; income from fixed-maturity securities rose 10.3%.
Net realized and unrealized investment results swung to a $17.5M loss from a $78.8M gain a year earlier.
Insurance segment gross and net premiums written grew 4.9% and 3.2%, with average rate increases excluding workers' compensation near 4.0%.
